case_title: ENGINEERING EXPORT PROMOTION COUNCIL v. USHA ANAND
neutral_facts: The accused, a merchant exporter of automotive components, was involved in cases registered against him and his three brothers by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) for offences under Sections 420, 468/471 of the Indian Penal Code. The accused deposited a sum of money with the appellant, a channelising industry under the Ministry of Commerce, and requested it to inform the CBI not to take any measures against him. The other three brothers also deposited similar amounts. The trial continued against all four, but the three brothers were eventually acquitted. The accused died before the trial concluded, leading to the abatement of the case against him. The acquitted brothers claimed a refund of the deposited money, which was granted by the trial court. The accused's wife then filed a similar claim on behalf of her late husband, which was allowed by the High Court. The appellant challenged the High Court's order, arguing that the money was deposited on the accused's own volition and not as a condition of bail, and that the High Court's exercise of its inherent power under Section 482 of the Code was inappropriate.
